correctness.rationale: The final claim uses the standard ten-vertex Petersen graph and faces with induced components of order at most two. An independently coded exhaustive traversal of all 2^10 vertex masks verifies 260 nonempty faces and f=(10,45,90,80,30,5). The explicit 0..9 toggle algorithm produces 128 disjoint cover matches and four critical masks 1,82,116,402 in dimensions 0,2,3,3; all 860 Hasse incidences are checked by topological sort. Independent exact signed gradient-path recursion yields Morse ∂3=(-1,-1), which as degree-one attaching maps cancels the single two-sphere leaving S^3. This proves the complete finite claim, not a pattern for other graphs or r.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is a canonical smallest cubic nonchordal benchmark for higher independence complexes. Its exact integral homotopy type and explicit nontrivial Morse differential fill a natural case omitted from earlier tractable graph-family classifications; the computation is reproducible and could serve as a benchmark. The significance is this independently useful exact homotopy invariant, not a fictitious general theorem.
